examples.name: dashboard-operations-capacity
examples.title: Operations · Capacity and exceptions
examples.description: Capacity planning for an operations team. A GaugeChart shows overall utilisation against planned hours, a StackedBarList splits capacity by team, and the work queue combines a FilterBar with Tabs that swap between modules and open exceptions. Choose it when the question is 'can we take on more work?'.

examples.name: dashboard-delivery-timesheet
examples.title: Project · Delivery timesheet
examples.description: A project page built around time, not charts. A Breadcrumb and Avatar group frame the project, Tabs move between views, StatCards summarise logged hours, utilisation and overtime, and a weekly worklog table steps backwards and forwards one week at a time.

examples.name: dashboard-agent-analytics
examples.title: AI agents · Conversation analytics
examples.description: A product-analytics view for an AI assistant. Tabs switch the main ComposedChart between conversations and model cost, a ranked list pairs each agent's ChatAgentMark with a Progress bar, and a DonutChart shows where conversations start. Use it when the subject is a set of agents rather than revenue or traffic.

examples.name: dashboard-edge-security
examples.title: Security · Edge telemetry
examples.description: A dense operations console for live telemetry. A region ToggleGroup filters threats by vector (BarChart), a SankeyChart traces network flow, Progress bars show cluster load, and the active-threats list lets an operator pause and resume a mitigation rule without leaving the page.

examples.name: dashboard-field-coverage
examples.title: Field teams · Coverage
examples.description: Built for teams in the field. StatCards report sites covered and staff on shift, a crews table uses Avatars for people, an action queue lets a manager approve hours inline, and a ComposedChart checks supply against forecast. It favours actions over analysis.

examples.name: dashboard-commerce-revenue
examples.title: Commerce · Revenue
examples.description: The classic revenue dashboard: StatCards with Sparklines, an AreaChart by product line that switches period with a segmented control, a BarChart channel mix, and an order queue in a DataTable whose row menu opens a Dialog. It is the most complete starting point for shop and SaaS metrics.

examples.name: dashboard-creator-payouts
examples.title: Creators · Payouts
examples.description: A money-out view for creators rather than a metrics overview. A claimable balance leads, a ComposedChart compares receipts with the reserve buffer, Switch rows set automatic payout sweeps, and a DataTable ledger records every movement. Claiming a balance updates the page in place.

examples.name: dashboard-newsletter-analytics
examples.title: Content · Newsletter analytics
examples.description: An editorial analytics page for a newsletter or blog. Subscriber growth (AreaChart), a FunnelChart for the last issue, a HeatmapChart of when readers open, a ChatActivityHistory feed of recent events and an issues table; a switch compares against the previous period. It is the reading-focused counterpart to the commerce dashboard.
